thread:
aj_sales: Heads-up — AcmeCorp POC is seeing slow TTFT and intermittent 429s over the last hour on their Dedicated trial. Can eng swarm?

katie_se: On it. Can you paste a failing request ID and the typical prompt size? Also are they on the JS SDK or direct API?

aj_sales: They're on the JS SDK v0.9.2. Sample request header from customer:
```
Request-ID: req_9b3f7a
prompt_tokens: ~180
model: redwood-xl-1b
client-session: session_abcd1234 (rotates each call currently)
```

aj_sales: Also getting multiple 429s in UI logs: "429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED" and UI shows slower first token (TTFT ~ 800-1200ms vs expected ~300-400ms).

tomas_infra: Looking at serving logs for dedicated-us-west-2 pool — seeing throttling spikes. Snippet: 
```
[2026-03-21T14:02:11Z] req=req_9b3f7a queue=dedicated-us-west-2 status=queued latency_ms=4200 error=RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
[2026-03-21T14:02:12Z] req=req_9b3f8b queue=dedicated-us-west-2 status=running latency_ms=1200
[2026-03-21T14:02:15Z] pool=dedicated-us-west-2 concurrency=38 max=40 queue_len=110
[2026-03-21T14:02:16Z] cache_miss=true kv_hit_rate=22%
```
tomas_infra: The pool concurrency is near max and queue length spikes coincide with many short prompts ==> batching mixing long+short requests. Also KV cache hit rate is low which makes TTFT worse.

maria_devex: Low KV hit rate + rotating session_id explains cache_miss. If each request uses a new session token we can't leverage prefix/KV caching. Their SDK config defaults to ephemeral session per call.

aj_sales: @maria_devex they confirmed session tokens rotate per request (they thought it was safer).

maria_devex: Short-term mitigation ideas: enforce session affinity (stable session_id per user), reduce interleaving of very short prompts, and set batching to avoid mixing long requests into the same batch as many short ones. Also suggest enabling prefix_cache for the pool.

katie_se: Sales/privacy note — customer asked whether enabling session affinity will cause any new data residency issues. Maria, is that just a client-side change?

maria_devex: Yes it's a client-side change: keep a stable session_id per conversation. No added server-side data residency changes.

aj_sales: Tomas, can infra apply any quick server-side mitigations while we get the SDK change rolled?

tomas_infra: Yes. Quick actions I'm proposing: 1) Temporarily reduce `max_concurrency` for dedicated-us-west-2 from 40 -> 28 to smooth spikes; 2) Turn on `prefix_cache=true` for that pool; 3) Adjust batching config to avoid combining >1 long prompt (>1024 tokens) with many short ones. Example config we'll push: 
```json
{
  "pool": "dedicated-us-west-2",
  "max_concurrency": 28,
  "prefix_cache": true,
  "batching": {
    "max_batch_tokens": 1024,
    "max_batch_size": 8,
    "prefer_latency_for_short_prompts": true
  }
}
```

ops-bot: ops-bot: change-request applied by tomas_infra — routing policy and pool config updated. ticket=RW-12345

aj_sales: Noted. Customer also asked a pricing question: if we cap concurrency or throttle, does that change their trial billing or committed cost? They want to know if we should expect higher cost from retrying due to 429s.

katie_se: I can own the billing answer on the call if we get an estimate.

maria_devex: Quick estimate based on their workload: before mitigation token/sec ~1500 -> after changes ~900. On Dedicated burst pricing for POC that equates to roughly +$120/day if we kept the same throughput via higher burst. But with the concurrency cap, throughput will drop and we likely save cost vs trying to scale. I'll DM the cost calc spreadsheet to @aj_sales.

aj_sales: Great, I'll schedule a sync with AcmeCorp for 11am PT and include the runbook + cost note. Will ask them to patch SDK to stable session_id before the call.

tomas_infra: Long term: we should update the JS SDK to make session affinity the default and add heuristic batching that separates short vs long prompts at runtime. I'll open a runtime PR and a devex PR for SDK docs. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/458 (will post updates).

maria_devex: Also recommending we add an alert: KV_hit_rate < 35% triggers early-warning so SEs can proactively flag POCs.

aj_sales: Thanks all — appreciated. I'll post the customer follow-up notes after the call. :thumbsup:
